newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Supported by rand S.African shares end slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Supported by rand S.African shares end slightly up.

text.p: South African shares finished barely up from their starting levels on Monday, but dealers said that overall trade was positive.
Shares traded in a very tight range throughout the day.

Industrials finished slightly firmer after gaining more ground earlier and thwarting market expectations that they would suffer a weaker day in the wake of Wall Street's Friday losses and bucking the trend of weaker world markets.
Dealers said that industrial shares found support from a strong rand and bond rates. The rand ended three cents firmer at the local close.
But gold shares were not as bright after the rand began to strengthen, dealers said.

Having suffered lately due to a vulnerable bullion price, the gold index hopped up when it appeared that bullion was safely sitting above the $353 an ounce level but these small gains soon shrank as the rand firmed.
The gold index added 4.9 points to 1,375.3 points, the all-share index put on 4.7 points to 6,689.3 and the industrial index was up 1.1 points at 8,043.9 points.
Dealers said that the local market would be eyeing Wall Street for direction on Tuesday.
